question: With the extra-inning runner on 2nd, does bunting the runner to 3rd pay, and has the home edge changed?
answer: No measurable edge either way; visitors' bunts -0.16 runs (CI -0.35 to +0.02). Home teams win 50.0% of extra games.
findings: Visitors, tied, leadoff bunt try vs swing: runs -0.16 (CI -0.35 to +0.02), win -1.2 pts (CI -9.3 to +6.5).
Home, tied, bunt try vs swing: scored -0.3 pts (CI -9.1 to +8.4), win +1.0 pts (CI -6.1 to +7.8).
Leadoff bunt attempt rate in extras: 13.9% of 3,132 halves; bunters hit -15 pts of wOBA vs swingers +4.
method: Leadoff PA of each extra half-inning (runner on 2nd, 0 out), non-pitchers. Bunt try = bunt in play or a foul/missed bunt. Linear model with batter-season wOBA and season; game bootstrap CIs. Intent beyond the batter is not observed.
data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2020-2025 regular season (7-inning games removed), 2,232 tied extra half-innings; 2015-19 extras for home win %. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).
split_check: Win diff, bunt minus swing: visitors -9.8 pts 2020-22, +1.9 2023-25; home +8.8, +0.4 (raw).
